answers: To report a Code of Conduct violation, you can submit an incident report to the Kubernetes Code of Conduct Committee. This can be done by emailing conduct@kubernetes.io [1]. You can also reach out via Slack direct messages to individual committee members, but they might direct you to contact them via email. [1]

An OWNERS file is used to designate responsibility over different parts of the Kubernetes codebase [1]. It applies to everything within a directory, including the OWNERS file itself, sibling files, and child directories [1][2]. The file is in YAML format and supports keys such as `approvers`, `reviewers`, and `labels` [2]. It is used to assign roles like reviewer and approver for code reviews [1].

OWNERS files in Kubernetes repositories are used to designate responsibility over different parts of the Kubernetes codebase [1]. They assign the reviewer and approver roles for the two-phase code review process [1].
